notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/cram2__semantic_digital_twin --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The card's family-config/MujocoDriver shape was used unchanged; no deviation. model_path points at the card's models[0], resources/mjcf/mjx_single_cube_no_mesh.xml, in the read-only clone at 40a35e7e481b358cd7f9d939c7ff4e0c23826098; nothing from the clone is imported or copied. The fake is this package's stand-in mujoco module (a factory callable), because MuJoCo is not installed where the gate runs. The bridge derives cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 over 16 qpos, 15 dof and 8 actuator ctrlranges: the seven arm position actuators plus the finger general actuator. actuator7 states no own ctrlrange, so the stand-in uses the panda general default -2.8973 to 2.8973 at model line 8, the MJCF position shortcut; fake.py and facts.md document that. The real MuJoCo engine and the upstream Multiverse adapter were not run, and the stand-in was not compared with an engine load. Warnings: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (the MuJoCo fake is a module factory, so the gate cannot record or compare a native class surface and describes it as an upstream simulator; the bridge-boundary checks still pass), and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (ticks, the reset seed and the mixed-unit action.ctrl vector, expected for a simulated world per PLAYBOOK.md section 8). There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue_requests. No hardware backend was run and no hardware run is claimed. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run; gate.digest is the stable digest the check printed.
